question: What is the life expectancy at birth for women in Japan, according to the 2023 official life table?
source_title: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (Japan) – Abridged Life Tables for Japan 2023
explainer: Japanese women have the longest life expectancy of any large population; Japanese men come in at about 81 years, a gap of roughly six years.

question: What was the median age at first marriage for men in the United States in 2023?
source_title: U.S. Census Bureau – Historical Marital Status Tables (Table MS-2)
explainer: American men now marry about seven years later than in 1960, when the median was 22.8; women's median in 2023 was 28.4.

question: How many official languages does the European Union have?
source_title: European Union – Languages
explainer: With 27 member states but 24 languages, every EU law is translated into all of them, and the European Parliament runs one of the largest interpreting services in the world.

question: What share of the world's population lived in urban areas in 2023?
source_title: World Bank – Urban population (% of total population)
explainer: Humanity crossed the 50% urban mark around 2007; the UN expects more than two-thirds of people to live in cities by 2050.

question: How many living languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea?
source_title: Ethnologue – Papua New Guinea
explainer: With under 10 million people, Papua New Guinea has more languages than any other country, roughly one in every nine languages on Earth.

question: On an average day in 2023, how many babies were born in Ireland?
source_title: Central Statistics Office (Ireland) – Vital Statistics Annual Report 2023
explainer: Ireland registered about 54,700 births in 2023, down from a peak of around 75,000 in 2009, so each day brings roughly 150 newborns.

question: How many living languages are there in the world, as counted by Ethnologue in 2024?
source_title: Ethnologue – How many languages are there in the world?
explainer: About 40% of those languages are endangered, while just 23 languages are spoken by more than half of the world's population.

question: On an average day in 2023, how many people died in Japan?
source_title: Wikipedia – Demographics of Japan (vital statistics)
explainer: Japan recorded about 1.58 million deaths in 2023 against only 727,000 births, so the population shrinks by more than 2,000 people every day.

question: How many baby boys born in the US in 2023 were named Liam, the year's most popular name?
source_title: Social Security Administration – Popular Baby Names
explainer: Liam has topped the US boys' list every year since 2017, yet it accounts for barely 1% of boys born, a sign of how much more varied naming has become since the 1950s.

question: What was the population of Greenland on 1 January 2024?
source_title: Statistics Greenland – Population
explainer: The world's largest island has fewer residents than a mid-sized town; about a third of them live in the capital, Nuuk.

question: On an average day in 2023, how many babies were born worldwide?
source_title: United Nations – World Population Prospects 2024
explainer: That is about 132 million births a year, or roughly 250 every minute, against about 61 million deaths.

question: How many people became naturalized US citizens in fiscal year 2023?
source_title: USCIS – Naturalization Statistics
explainer: FY2023 was one of the busiest years for naturalizations in US history; Mexico, India and the Philippines were the top countries of origin.

question: What was the population of the Republic of Ireland in April 2024?
source_title: Central Statistics Office (Ireland) – Population and Migration Estimates, April 2024
explainer: Ireland's population passed 5 million in 2021 for the first time since the Great Famine of the 1840s, driven mostly by immigration.

question: How many international students were enrolled at US colleges and universities in the 2023/24 academic year?
source_title: Open Doors 2024 – International Students
explainer: A record year: India overtook China as the top sending country, and international students made up about 6% of all US higher-education enrolment.

question: What was Australia's population on 30 June 2024?
source_title: Australian Bureau of Statistics – National, state and territory population, June 2024
explainer: Australia's population grew by about half a million in a single year, the bulk of it from overseas migration, on a landmass the size of the contiguous US.

question: How many Jews were there in the world in 2023 (core Jewish population)?
source_title: Wikipedia – Jewish population by country (Jewish Agency / DellaPergola estimates)
explainer: The world Jewish population still has not regained its 1939 level of about 16.6 million; Israel and the United States account for roughly 85% of the total.

question: How many international migrants (people living outside the country they were born in) were there worldwide in 2024?
source_title: UN DESA – International Migrant Stock 2024
explainer: Migrants are about 3.7% of humanity; if they formed one country it would be the fourth most populous on Earth.

question: What was the population of Indonesia in mid-2023?
source_title: Wikipedia – Demographics of Indonesia (Statistics Indonesia / BPS estimates)
explainer: Indonesia is the world's fourth most populous country, and more than half its people live on the single island of Java.

question: How many children and youth worldwide were out of school in 2023, according to UNESCO?
source_title: UNESCO – 250 million children out-of-school: What you need to know about UNESCO's latest education data
explainer: That is roughly one in six school-age children and youth; sub-Saharan Africa accounts for about 30% of them.

question: How many Muslims were there in the world in 2020?
source_title: Pew Research Center – How the Global Religious Landscape Changed from 2010 to 2020
explainer: Muslims were about a quarter of humanity in 2020 and the fastest-growing major religious group; Indonesia, Pakistan and India have the largest Muslim populations.

question: How many people worldwide spoke English as a first or second language in 2024?
source_title: Ethnologue – What are the top 200 most spoken languages?
explainer: Only about 380 million of them are native speakers; the rest learned English as an additional language, which is why it edges out Mandarin as the most spoken language overall.

question: How many humans have ever been born in all of history, up to 2022?
source_title: Population Reference Bureau – How Many People Have Ever Lived on Earth?
explainer: About 7% of everyone who has ever lived is alive today, so the claim that the living outnumber the dead is a myth.

question: How much money did migrants send home in remittances to low- and middle-income countries in 2023?
source_title: World Bank – Remittances Slowed in 2023, Expected to Grow Faster in 2024
explainer: Remittances now exceed foreign direct investment and official aid to developing countries; India alone received about US$120 billion.

question: What was the total outstanding student loan debt in the United States at the end of 2023?
source_title: Federal Reserve Bank of New York – Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit, Q4 2023
explainer: Student loans are the second-largest category of US household debt after mortgages, spread across roughly 43 million borrowers, about US$37,000 each.
